text:
maria: heads-up — us-west1 spot-gpu pool preemptions spiked to ~18% over the last 10m, causing a flurry of restarts for long-running infer jobs

jake: saw the alert. autoscaler didn't create new nodes fast enough?

infra-bot: [alert] cluster-autoscaler: scaleUpFailed (insufficient quota) for nodepool/gpu-usw1-spot at 2391234570

sasha: quota message rings true — GCP returned RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED for GPUs a few times when I checked the API logs

maria: exact problem: provisioning rate throttled, then K8s queued pods. When spot nodes came back they were overloaded and we hit eviction cascade

kai: proposal: introduce an "evacuation-lane" tainted standby group (taint=evacuation-lane=true:NoSchedule) sized to absorb 15% of concurrent GPU pods. warm nodes with taint so normal scheduling won't use them unless we Tolerate + tolerate-key=evacuation

jake: neat. so GPU jobs would be moved to evacuation-lane via patching PodSpec tolerations during drain? feels risky to mutate user pod specs in-flight

sasha: another approach: split queue by job-length. short interactive latency-critical pods keep using spot pool; long batch jobs prefer on-demand fallback pool. implement via topology/affinity or scheduler policy in queueing layer

oliver: quick mitigation we rolled previously: increase cluster-autoscaler --max-node-provision-time and add a short prewarm of 2 nodes on-demand on scale events to avoid single-event capacity cliffs

maria: can we also lower the drain grace period? current eviction drain default is 5m and stack pileups. shorter drain + priority eviction for best-effort batch reduces head-of-line blocking

kai: draft runbook snippet:
```
# eviction-lane play
1) set gpustandby nodepool desired=3 (tainted evacuation-lane)
2) kubectl cordon <victim-node>
3) kubectl drain <victim-node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=60
4) patch pods with toleration only for migration-controller
```

jake: also we need an alert on metric: nodepool_provision_rate < threshold AND preempt_count spike. right now we only alert on total preempt_count which is noisy

sasha: agree. add metric: cpu/gpu_provision_latency P95 and alert when > 20s combined with preempt rate > 5% over 5m

maria: ops action list for today: 1) enable a 2-node on-demand warm pool in us-west1 for 3h window (manual) 2) create evacuation-lane nodepool PR with taint and small desired 3) add prometheus alerts for provision_rate and provision_latency 4) test queue-splitting on staging

infra-bot: action created: GH#4821 (evacuation-lane nodepool + alerts) by maria — due today

oliver: I'll take the PR for nodepool config. sasha can you own prometheus alert rule? jake can you test scaleUp timing with simulated churn?

maria: thanks team — we'll reconvene after the staging run. :thumbsup:
